title: Iter-3 price-injection breaks ASK side: high bit (bit 127) not stripped before >>64
description: The iter-3 patch sets Order.price = Number(BigInt(orderIdStr) >> 64n) for every order, then computeMarketStats prefers o.price over the decode fallback. This decode is correct for bids (high bit clear) but wrong for asks: chain-shape.md's captured Order has order_id '170141183460486719245069180370816077150' with bit 127 set (per the convention 'asks the encoding is monotonically increasing'); decoding gives 170141183460486719245069180370816077150n >> 64n = 9223372036855723808n ≈ 9.22e18, NOT the real price 948000. Verified empirically against the captured Order in chain-shape.md line 129. The previous decodeAskPrice (id & (ASK_BIT-1n)) >> 64n correctly produced 948000 by stripping the high bit first; iter-3 silently bypasses that fallback by always populating price with the broken value (still finite, still passes the `if (!Number.isFinite(price)) price = undefined` guard). Net effect: bestAsk = ~9.22e18 on every real-chain card, midPrice = (~9.22e18 + bidPrice)/2 ≈ ~4.6e18, AC1.4's bestBid<=mid<=bestAsk technically holds but mid is astronomically wrong, depth at +/-1% from a ~4.6e18 mid sums to 0 (no real level lies in [4.55e18, 4.65e18]). This is a strict regression vs iter-2: iter-2 broke bids and asks worked; iter-3 'fixes' bids and now breaks asks. The CR-2 cluster is not closed; it has migrated.
impact: AC1.4 invariant trivially holds but mid/spread/depth values are nonsense once any ask exists on the sandbox. Tests pass tautologically because marketStats.test.ts never injects price (it tests the fallback path) and networkShape.test.ts (T-014) returns empty BigVector dynamic-field lists so traverseBigVector returns [] before hitting the new code. The fix looks complete to the test gate but is broken on real chain data — the same 'load-bearing fix is untriggered by tests' shape iter-2 R1-001 called out, with the failure mode now on the OTHER side of the book.
recommendation: Replace `Number(BigInt(orderIdStr) >> 64n)` with `Number((BigInt(orderIdStr) & ((1n << 127n) - 1n)) >> 64n)` to strip the ask high bit before extracting the upper-64 price. Add a regression test that constructs an ask Order using `makeAskOrderId(948n, 1n)` (from marketStats.test.ts), passes it through traverseBigVector's logic (extract via a small unit-testable helper), and asserts the injected price is 948 — not 9.22e18. The captured chain-shape.md sample (order_id 170141183460486719245069180370816077150, expected price 948000) is the canonical regression fixture. Optional: also assert `price < 10**15` defensively and fall through to undefined if not, so the next encoding drift crashes the card loudly rather than silently rendering 4.6e18.

title: fetchPoolStats silently degrades to empty book on malformed RPC response (iter-2 R1-002 unaddressed)
description: Iter-2 finding carried forward unchanged. resolvePoolInnerFields returns null silently when sui_getObject's content.fields is missing/null (extractFields → null) and several intermediate cases (no inner field, no versioned id, empty dynamic-fields, no wrapperFields) `return fields` (degraded) or `return null` without surfacing the failure. fetchPoolStats then constructs a default-empty PoolInnerState (line 350) and computeMarketStats yields all-undefined card stats — visually indistinguishable from 'pool is genuinely idle'. Iter-3 did not touch this. rpc() (line 56) still calls response.json() without checking response.ok; a 502/503 from the RPC during sandbox restart parses HTML as JSON and throws SyntaxError that reaches the per-pool error banner verbatim ('Unexpected token <').
impact: Operators cannot distinguish 'idle market' from 'shape parse failure' from 'sandbox restarted with new package shape'. Same silent-failure pattern as the iter-1 CR-1 cluster, partially carried forward.
recommendation: Add `if (!response.ok) throw new Error(\`${method} HTTP ${response.status}: ${await response.text()}\`)` between fetch and json() in rpc(). In resolvePoolInnerFields and buildPoolInnerState, throw an actionable error when expected fields are absent rather than returning a degraded shape. App.tsx's allSettled banner already handles propagated errors.

title: Versioned->PoolInner traversal branch is still untested (iter-2 R1-004 unaddressed)
description: Iter-2 finding carried forward unchanged. resolvePoolInnerFields has two cases: (1) the response already has a 'book' field — return directly (T-014 fixture path); (2) Pool wrapper → Versioned dynamic field → PoolInner field-wrapper traversal — the only path that runs against the real sandbox. The T-014 fixture in networkShape.test.ts always returns case (1) (it stubs sui_getObject with a `content.fields.book` shape and stubs suix_getDynamicFields with `data: []`), so case (2) — including the wrapperFields['value']?.['fields'] unwrap shape derived from chain-shape.md Step 3 — has zero test coverage. Iter-3 did not add coverage. Note: this is the same blind spot that masked the iter-3 R1-001 ask-bit defect — T-014 returns empty dynamic-field arrays, so the new price-injection code path is also unexercised.
impact: Production-only data path (case 2 traversal + traverseBigVector with non-empty slices) has zero unit-test coverage. A Sui RPC drift in the value-shape unwrap, or in dynamic-field response shape, would silently produce empty books with no actionable signal AND silently mask further injection bugs.
recommendation: Promote the chain-shape.md Step 1-3 captures to JSON fixtures under tests/fixtures/. Add a test that primes the fetch spy with the real Versioned wrapper shape and asserts (a) buildPoolInnerState extracts asks/bids BigVector ids correctly and (b) traverseBigVector populates Order.price correctly for both an ask Order (high bit set, expected price=948000) and a bid Order (high bit clear, expected price=671000) — using the captured order_ids from chain-shape.md as fixture inputs.

title: App polling effect lacks tick-id/abort guard; stale tick can overwrite fresh state (iter-2 R1-008 unaddressed)
description: Iter-2 finding carried forward unchanged. The polling useEffect runs setInterval(20s) and Promise.allSettled over all pools per tick. There is no guard against the previous tick still being in-flight: if a per-pool fetchPoolStats takes >20s (entirely possible during BigVector slice churn per chain-shape.md friction note), tick N+1 starts before tick N's setState commits. Both ticks resolve in arbitrary order; setState applies last-writer-wins, which may be the older request. There is also no AbortController for unmount cleanup; setState may fire on an unmounted component. Iter-3 did not address this.
impact: Sparkline freshness AC (AC1.5) intermittently violated under slow/concurrent ticks: a slow fetch can overwrite a more recent fast fetch with stale data. Possible React 'state update on unmounted component' warning if unmount happens during a tick.
recommendation: Track a per-tick AbortController; abort it when the next tick starts or component unmounts. Alternatively, use a monotonically increasing tick-id captured at tick start and only commit setState if the resolved tick is the latest.

title: Cross-pool event throughput unbounded; fetchFills can paginate forever on busy sandbox (iter-2 R1-007 unaddressed)
description: Iter-2 finding carried forward unchanged. buildQueryEventsFn issues suix_queryEvents with MoveModule filter on `module: 'pool'` (correctly per chain-shape.md friction note), which returns events from ALL pools in the package. fillFetcher demultiplexes via `if (ev.poolId !== poolId) continue;` (good), but the page-cap stop conditions (`collected.length >= MAX_FILLS` or `crossedWindow`) only trigger on OUR pool's events. If our target pool is sparse and competing pools are busy, every 50-event page may yield 0 of our events, and fillFetcher paginates until hasNextPage:false — which on a continuously-active sandbox may be effectively never. The 20s refresh tick can be exceeded. Iter-3 did not address this.
impact: Under sandbox event contention, a single fetchFills invocation can issue hundreds of RPC calls and exceed the 20s refresh interval, compounding with R1-004 to overwrite fresh state with very stale data.
recommendation: Add a hard pagination ceiling (e.g. MAX_PAGES = 20) to fillFetcher and surface a one-line warning on hit. Or restructure to issue one suix_queryEvents per refresh and demultiplex events to all pools in a single pass instead of N queries per N pools.

title: rpc() does not check response.ok; non-2xx surfaces confusing JSON-parse errors (iter-2 R1-006 unaddressed)
description: Iter-2 finding carried forward unchanged. rpc() calls fetch then immediately response.json() without checking response.ok. If Sui RPC returns 502/503 (e.g., during sandbox restart) the response body is HTML; response.json() throws SyntaxError 'Unexpected token < in JSON at position 0'. This reaches App.tsx's per-pool error banner verbatim — confusing and not actionable. Failure is observable, not silent — but the error text is misleading. Iter-3 did not address this.
impact: Operator-facing error text quality during sandbox restart. Not a correctness regression; UX paper-cut.
recommendation: Add `if (!response.ok) throw new Error(\`${method} HTTP ${response.status}\`);` between fetch and json().

title: chain-shape.md decoding note is internally contradictory; types.ts comment perpetuates the wrong half
description: chain-shape.md states two things about the bid encoding that cannot both be true: (1) 'for bids it's [the encoding is] decreasing (inverted price), so a sort by raw order_id ascending lists ... bids worst-first' AND (2) 'price is the upper 64 bits; the lower 64 bits are an order-counter disambiguator'. Empirically the captured bid order_id 12377783720203182843884075 has high-64 = 671000 = real price (plain), and low-64 = U64_MAX - 3540 (inverted counter, so descending sort puts newest bid first). So statement (2) is correct for the price half, statement (1) is correct for the COUNTER (not the price) — but the marketStats.test.ts fixture builder makeBidOrderId encodes ((U64_MAX - price) << 64) | counter, which contradicts (2) and matches (1) misread as price-inverted. The test fixture's encoding is inconsistent with the captured chain shape; tests pass against the fixture's own builder by tautology. types.ts comment line 8 echoes 'bid prices are stored inverted as U64_MAX - price' which is the same wrong reading. This documentation drift is the upstream root cause of both the iter-2 CR-2 (`decodeBidPrice` defined for the wrong inversion) and the iter-3 R1-001 (the `>> 64n` shortcut, which is correct for bids and wrong for asks because the author conflated the two cases).
impact: Future authors will keep getting this wrong until the note is rewritten. The iter-2 critical and iter-3 critical both have this single root cause.
recommendation: Rewrite chain-shape.md lines 136-145 to: 'order_id u128 layout: bit 127 = ask flag (1=ask, 0=bid); bits 64-126 = price (plain integer, NOT inverted, on both sides); bits 0-63 = order counter (ASKS use ascending counter; BIDS use U64_MAX - counter so newest bid sorts first under ascending raw-id sort within a price level). To extract price: (id & ((1<<127)-1)) >> 64. The captured samples (ASK order_id 170141183460486719245069180370816077150 → price 948000; BID order_id 12377783720203182843884075 → price 671000) are the regression fixtures.' Also fix marketStats.test.ts makeBidOrderId to NOT invert price, and fix types.ts line 8 comment.
evidence:
**Critical decoding note (sui-sdk + deepbook):** `order_id` is a u128 returned
by RPC as a decimal string. The high bits encode the limit price. For asks the
encoding is monotonically increasing in price; for bids it's decreasing
(inverted price), so a sort by raw `order_id` ascending lists asks
best-first / bids worst-first. The price itself can also be derived from the
event stream (`OrderPlaced.price`) or by decoding bits 64-127 of the u128
(price is the upper 64 bits; the lower 64 bits are an order-counter
disambiguator).

title: Polling refresh does not reload manifest; cachedPackageId stale across sandbox restart (iter-2 R1-005 unaddressed)
description: Iter-2 finding carried forward unchanged. main.tsx caches cachedPackageId at first loadManifest and never re-reads it. The App.tsx periodic refresh effect calls fetchPoolStats which uses the cached packageId. If the sandbox restarts mid-session and emits a new packageId, the SPA keeps querying the old packageId — suix_queryEvents filtered to a non-existent module returns zero events; cards continue to render but the sparkline silently freezes. Same silent-failure shape as iter-1 CR-1 in micro.
impact: AC1.5 freshness fails silently after a sandbox restart with no UI signal.
recommendation: Either (a) reload the manifest as part of the polling cycle and feed packageId via props, or (b) log a console.warn once when cachedPackageId is '' on a fetchPoolStats call so the silent-zero case at least leaves a trail.
